ACTION: Read `~/.claude/skills/subagent-driven-development/references/fix-loop.md`. I re-read it before every fix round, and it decides who fixes round 5, how the re-review runs, and what adjudication follows if round 5 fails.

ACTION: Dispatch the round 5 fix subagent for Task 6 with model `fable`, following fix-loop.md's resume-vs-fresh rule. The prompt is the Task 6 brief file from `scripts/task-brief`, not the whole plan. It also carries the global constraints and finding F1 verbatim: "The invalidation still races with the background refresh in `cache/refresh.py:88`; the new test passes only because it never starts the refresh thread." The prompt asks for two things: a fix that removes the race at `cache/refresh.py:88`, and a test that starts the real refresh thread and fails without the fix. It also includes the round 4 report, which says the lock was added but was not enough.

ACTION: When round 5 reports, generate a fresh review package with `scripts/review-package` and dispatch the scoped re-review from `re-review-prompt.md`. Use at least standard, and capable here because the change is concurrency-related. If F1 is still open after that, adjudicate as fix-loop.md describes. That is the fifth and last attempt.

**Message to partner:**

Task 6 is still open. The round 4 re-review found that the invalidation still races with the background refresh at `cache/refresh.py:88`. The new test passes only because it never starts the refresh thread. That was a thorough attempt by opus at high effort, so I'm dispatching round 5, the last allowed attempt, to `fable`. It must fix the race and add a test that runs the real refresh thread. A scoped re-review follows. I'll report back when Task 6 resolves, or sooner if round 5 fails and it goes to adjudication.
